title: Climate Change and Mutual Fund Voting on Climate Proposals
authors: Alberta Di Giuli; Alexandre Garel; Roni Michaely; Arthur Romec
publication: Management Science 72(2), 1253-1276 (February 2026); Articles in Advance May 30, 2025
rescreened_nov4: Earlier record was unassessable: the package download was incomplete (.part, no central directory) and there was no article text. Re-screened from the published article text (data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2022.03733.txt) and the complete 810 MB package (76 archive entries, unpacked by the intake into package_dir): Readme.rtf, 'Stata - 7. Empirical analysis.do' and the intake inventory data/packages/mnsc.2022.03733_regressions.txt.
near_miss_reason: Stacked difference-in-differences in every main-text column (Cengiz et al. 2019, following Baker et al. 2022). For each year-quarter of a first abnormal-heat shock, the authors build a cohort with the climate-proposal votes of first-shocked funds and never-shocked clean controls in the four quarters before and after the shock (shock quarter omitted). They stack 11 cohorts (2010Q1-2021Q2) and estimate reghdfe vote_for treated##post with cohort-fund and cohort-proposal FE (Tables 2-7; Table 2 Panel C and Table 9 use cohort-fund with cohort-year-quarter or cohort-firm-year-quarter FE). Every column also includes the time-varying fund controls Ln(TNA) and Avg. Turnover Ratio. Table 2 Panel B and Tables 4-7 and 9 add triple interactions of Treated x Post with proposal, firm or fund characteristics. The underlying design is a staggered binary adoption: first exposure of the fund's headquarters city to a quarterly abnormal temperature above 2 degrees C, absorbing, at fund-specific quarters, with never-treated funds. No unstacked unit and calendar-time FE column is reported; the Table B.3 robustness columns are stacked too.
eligible_reason: No main-text column satisfies every rule. All DiD regressions are stacked with cohort-specific FE (not eligible) and include time-varying fund controls; the heterogeneity tables add triple interactions. Table 8 regresses proposal-level support on the continuous share of shocked funds with firm-year FE (not a DiD).
design_notes: ISS Voting Analytics fund votes on shareholder proposals, 2006-2022, matched to CRSP mutual funds through SEC N-PX fund series; fund headquarters zip codes from CRSP; NOAA GSOD station temperatures. Abnormal temperature = monthly temperature minus the average for that calendar month over the previous 10 years, averaged over the quarter. Treated = first quarter with average abnormal temperature above 2 degrees C. Cohorts start after the first three sample years; cohorts with less than 1% treated votes are dropped. Main sample: 31,453 votes on 568 climate proposals (31,115 in the baseline regression). Outcome: Vote For (0/100). Linear probability model; SEs two-way clustered by cohort-fund and cohort-proposal. Headline: Table 2 Panel A column 3, 11.170 (2.245). Code in 'Stata - 7. Empirical analysis.do': lines 244/268/298/335 (Table 2A), 361/384 (2B), 414-420 (2C), 608/612 (Table 3 loops), 648-723 (Tables 4-7), 804-814 (Table 8), 1019-1023 (Table 9), 1208-1235 (Table B.3).
